key_insight: In QAOA/VQE, optimizer success depends less on how many local minima exist and more on whether different basins lead to similar or very different objective values.
engineering_relevance: This helps choose between multistart local search and global evolutionary optimization when designing variational quantum workflows under a fixed function-evaluation budget.
method: Visualized the objective landscape by sampling directions and counting local minima.
Compared multistart BFGS against adaptive differential evolution (jSO) under matched evaluation budgets.
Studied how circuit depth, parameter tying, frustration, mixed locality, and reparameterization reshape the landscape in VQE and QAOA.
evidence_signal: Across VQE and QAOA experiments, deeper circuits increased sampled local-minimum counts, while parameter tying created larger quality gaps between local-search endpoints and made jSO outperform multistart BFGS.
watch_item: Local-minimum counts alone are not enough for solver selection; the key risk is assuming global search helps when basins are actually similarly good.
paper_title: Optimization Geometry of QAOA and Variational Quantum Algorithms
